items.title: Mr. Show: the fictional band
items.text: Start with the season-one opening episode, “The Cry of a Hungry Baby.” The name existed in sketch comedy before it became a recording project. Only the cameo is needed; a free official clip was not verified.
items.dateNote: Episode air date; background, not an album. Search link is not a verified official upload.

items.title: REV 22:20 — Underworld version
items.text: The first recorded Puscifer: Maynard James Keenan and Danny Lohner. Hear the soundtrack recording before the later album arrangement. The linked EP preserves the early version.

items.title: REV 22:20 (4:20 Mix)
items.text: The Saw II soundtrack remix is an early demonstration of the project’s habit of treating a song as material that can keep changing.

items.title: The Undertaker (Renholdër Mix)
items.text: The Underworld: Evolution contribution predates the debut album. Compare it with the later V Is for Vagina recording.

items.title: Cuntry Boner (Live)
items.text: The official description dates this live performance to 1999; the channel upload came in 2007. A comedy-era performance, distinct from the full Puscifer concert debut in 2009.
items.dateNote: Sorted by the public channel upload (15 September 2007). The official description dates the filmed performance to 1999.

items.title: Cuntry Boner - Single
items.text: The original single pairs Cuntry Boner (Evil Joe Barresi Mix) with the Circle Jerks cover World Up My Ass (Alan Moulder Mix). Both sit outside the standard debut album.

items.title: Queen B — Meats Meier animation
items.text: The first official video (2007): CGI chess and an early visual identity. This official upload is a later repost.
items.dateNote: Video was public by 4 October 2007; official description calls it the first video (2007). Linked official repost is dated 22 June 2011.

items.title: Don’t Shoot the Messenger
items.text: The four-track bridge from soundtrack experiments to a full catalog: two REV 22:20 versions, The Undertaker, and Trekka. The early soundtrack recordings above recur here.

items.title: V Is for Vagina
items.text: Studio album 01. Low-end electronics, deadpan delivery and bodily comedy establish the first vocabulary. Listen all the way through; Queen B, Momma Sed and The Undertaker are useful landmarks.
items.dateNote: Original album date. Deluxe edition is an alternative, not another required listen.
